answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprinting. Each agent’s action embeddings are hashed into a stable behavioural signature per epoch; a new identity must show trajectory continuity with its prior signature, measured as a bounded delta against its own history. Discontinuity triggers rate limits and a cooldown in a quarantine oasis until continuity is re-established. Sybil clusters cannot fake continuity without sustaining costly long-horizon behaviour, and each forged identity adds pigment of inconsistency that raises recomputation and delay costs.
